whatItFakes: Another state's budget year after the opening is its Census base moved line by line by the state's own base (jobs times pay, prices) and tax rates in force, with spending balanced to revenue; no act of the legislature adds to a spending line, no treasury, reserve or federal formula beyond the Medicaid match moves anything, and no money is paid.
why: Only the town's chain has treasuries and a budget process; the other states' legislatures pass acts as results (world-legislating) and no budget bill yet.
replacement: Each spending line moved by the state's enacted acts and formulas (aid rules, enrollment, caseload), reserves and debt service, and the legislature's budget act as a result; money paid when a state is opened.

whatItFakes: A disaster elsewhere in the country is one result row (state, kind, start day, number of counties) taken from the matching season of FEMA's recorded history 2000-2024 under the world's one seeded starting shift, cycling when the record runs out; it has no damage, no aid, no declaration and no reaction, and nothing reads it yet but the record log.
why: Damage should come from the housing stock, building codes, levees and budgets in force, the declaration from the governor's and the President's decisions, and aid from real treasuries (CTO ruling, Nov 8, 12:21 on #7365); those engines exist only for the town.
replacement: Detail built on open from the housing, budget and executive engines (damage, aid, the governor's and President's declarations), severity from the state's recorded spread, and the national press and approval reading the result.

whatItFakes: The country's disasters are FEMA's recorded 2000-2024 disasters replayed on their own days under one seeded starting shift, cycling every 25 years; after the record ends (Oct 9, 2026) the game does not make its own weather.
why: The zero-dice guard allows no new draw, and the hazard calendar after the record needs a GENERATION entry in the list-pick inventory and per-county monthly hazard rates, which are not built (owner, Oct 16: both FEMA's records and the world's own conditions; after the records end, the game keeps making its own weather).
replacement: Real FEMA disasters on their real dates while the world's dates fall inside the record (through Oct 9, 2026); after that a hazard calendar generated once at world creation from each county's recorded per-hazard monthly rates (a GENERATION entry), later fed by the world's own conditions (heat, drought).

whatItFakes: Another state's ballot measure result is kept as a result and enacts its law, but the press does not print the result itself: the measure-result bank has no place slot, so it would read as local news.
why: The English engine's measure-result pieces say "Voters approved {purpose}" with no place; the law the measure enacts reaches the national press through the law-took-effect story.
replacement: Measure-result bank pieces with a place (Words and Story), then this early return is deleted.

whatItFakes: The climate keeps one national warming level and each hazard's level month by month from the carbon laws in force, but no disaster reads a level yet: the real FEMA disasters replay as before and a hazard level moves nothing a player can see.
why: The owner's weather ruling (Nov 8) is built in three pieces: the links and the warming, each county's hazard levels, then disasters drawn from them; this is the first.
replacement: Each county's hazard level by season from its recorded history, moved by hazardFactor; disasters drawn month by month from those levels.

whatItFakes: The warming-to-hazard links use one size for every county: drought from the Southwest's vapor-pressure rise, wildfire from western forest studies, heat from a doubling over half a degree (no range); storm and flood from global and national figures converted to a per-degree size.
why: The National Climate Assessment and IPCC pages could not be fetched, and no source found gives a United States per-degree figure for heat, wildfire or drought by region or season.
replacement: Sizes by region and season from the National Climate Assessment (2023) chapters and the Littell et al. (2009) ecoprovince figure.

whatItFakes: The rest of the world's fossil CO2 follows a straight line between three published points (38.1 Gt in 2025, 35 in 2035, 30 in 2050, held flat after) and does not respond to any other country's law, price or event; its spread (flat near 38 Gt under current policies) is not run.
why: No year-by-year published scenario path was reachable; the IEA pages returned 403 and the points come from a search summary.
replacement: The IEA or IPCC scenario table by year, with other countries' own laws moving their share.
